content: Newborn children are soft and tender. When dead, they are stiff and hard. Ten thousand plants are soft and flexible. When dead, they are dry and brittle.
author: Lao Tzu
sourceWork: Tao Te Ching, Book of Virtue
story:
Serving as royal archivist during the moral disintegration of the Eastern Zhou Dynasty, Lao Tzu grew disillusioned with political intrigue and artificial societal rituals. Legend tells that before vanishing into the western wilderness atop a water buffalo, the border guard Yinxi persuaded him to record the timeless paradoxes of nature, effortless action (Wu Wei), and yielding strength.

In formulating this reflection, Lao Tzu stripped away superficial conventions to address the core anatomy of life. For Lao Tzu, true wisdom is never an abstract luxury, but an urgent practical discipline required to navigate life with clarity and unshakeable dignity.
reflectionPrompt: In what area of your life are you overthinking the ideal approach instead of taking the simple, honorable action?
